reply_text:
I found no dated AI predictions by Satya Nadella from 2019. Nothing I opened from that year meets all four tests.

- **Microsoft's speech pages for Build, Ignite and Inspire 2019** contain no speech text. Each page only links to a transcript file. I opened the Ignite (4 Nov 2019) and Inspire (17 July 2019) transcript PDFs but not the Build 2019 transcript, which is a .docx file, so that keynote hasn't been checked.
- **The Ignite and Inspire transcripts have dated forecasts, but none is about what AI will do.** Ignite has "50 billion devices by 2030, and 175 zettabytes of data by 2025". Inspire has tech spending "going to double by 2030 to 10 percent" of GDP and "50 billion connected devices by 2030". These are forecasts about devices, data and the tech market, so I left them out. The only forward line about AI ("AI and machine learning is being infused into every experience in a deep way, and you're going to see a lot of that") has no date.
- **The July 2019 Microsoft–OpenAI press release** has a Nadella quote about "democratizing" AI. It gives no date and says nothing about when AGI might come.
- **One lead I couldn't check:** a July 2019 Psychology Today search snippet says Nadella was "optimistic" about building the supercomputer and "the AGI on top of it". That seems to come from his recorded conversation with Sam Altman. I only saw it in a search snippet and had no page openings left, so it's not quoted below and not listed as undated. As described, it gives no timeline.

**Not checked:** the Build 2019 transcript, the Davos 2019 conversation (video only), and the Nadella–Altman video. I used 9 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings, so 3 searches are unused. The other 2019 earnings calls and the Mobile World Congress (MWC) 2019 keynote transcript also weren't opened.
